derivations_en:
Status: DRAFT; full N0007 formalization NOT_RUN. No shell, Lean, or LaTeX execution is claimed. This is a nonblind audit of the serialized statements and code, not an independent blind reconstruction. The supplied Lean auxiliaries do not certify N0007.

1. The representative issue must be settled at the level of definitions.

There are two mathematically different interpretations of the displayed regularity assertion (1.8):

(A) There is one measurable, locally integrable function w representing the distributional derivative ∂ₜu; ∇w is its distributional spatial gradient; and √ρ w is the weighted function appearing in (1.8).

(B) The weighted quantity and spatial gradient are unrelated functions obtained as approximation limits, without identification with a common distributional derivative.

Interpretation (A) is the ordinary weak-derivative reading of the notation in (1.8). Under that reading, existence of a common representative is part of the meaning of the original regularity assertion, rather than a further theorem or stronger regularity assumption. Interpretation (B) does not supply that assertion. Definition 1.1 by itself does not resolve this difference: the conservative equation contains ∂ₜ(ρu), not explicitly ∂ₜu. Nor can ∇uₜ ∈ L² alone resolve it, since a distribution depending only on time has zero spatial gradient.

Accordingly, a faithful Lean definition may specify the weak-derivative identities for the quantities explicitly denoted by derivatives in (1.8). It must not contain the desired material-source equation, a product-rule conclusion, or the desired spatial weak stress identity. If the parent instead has only separate approximation-limit objects, their identification is a genuine missing source/application theorem. The supplied source excerpts do not prove that identification, and this audit does not claim that they do.

A suitable defining identity for a common representative wᵢ is

    ∫∫ uᵢ ∂ₜψ = −∫∫ wᵢ ψ

for every ψ ∈ C_c^∞(R² × (0,T)), together with local integrability of wᵢ and the corresponding spatial weak-derivative identity for its listed gradient. Weighted membership must apply to the function √ρ wᵢ itself. These identities express derivative notation; they do not assume momentum cancellation.

2. First missing analytic lemma under interpretation (A).

The earliest indispensable missing analytic result in the representative-to-product-rule route is the following weighted local coercivity and regularity lemma. It must precede any use of uₜ ∈ L²_t H¹_loc.

\begin{lemma}[Weighted local coercivity]
Let B \subset \mathbb R^2 be a bounded ball, M,c>0, and let r be measurable with 0\le r\le M almost everywhere and \int_B r\ge c. Suppose v\in L^1(B), its distributional gradient belongs to L^2(B), and \sqrt r\,v\in L^2(B). Then v\in H^1(B) and
\[
 \|v\|_{L^2(B)}\le C(B,c,M)
 \bigl(\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(B)}+\|\sqrt r\,v\|_{L^2(B)}\bigr).
\]
The constant is independent of r and v.
\end{lemma}

Proof. First establish the unweighted assertion: if v ∈ L¹(B) and its weak gradient is in L²(B), then v ∈ H¹(B) and

    ‖v−v_B‖₂ ≤ C_B ‖∇v‖₂,
    v_B = |B|⁻¹ ∫_B v.

One non-circular proof uses concentric inner balls B_n increasing to B. Mollification on B_n gives smooth approximants with gradients bounded in L²(B_n). Their means converge by L¹ convergence. Poincaré therefore bounds the approximants in H¹(B_n); weak compactness and distributional convergence identify v as the H¹ limit. Thus the ordinary Poincaré inequality holds on each B_n. The constants can be bounded uniformly because the radii of B_n stay between half the radius of B and its full radius. Moreover v_{B_n} → v_B by L¹ integrability and |B_n| → |B|. Fatou's lemma gives the asserted inequality on B, and hence v ∈ L²(B). This argument must be formalized; it is not an invocation of weighted coercivity before H¹ membership is known.

Set m=∫_B r, A=‖√r v‖₂, and D=‖∇v‖₂. Since r²≤Mr,

    m |v_B|
      ≤ |∫_B rv| + ∫_B r|v−v_B|
      ≤ √m A + √(Mm) C_B D.

Consequently

    |v_B| ≤ c^(−1/2) A + √(M/c) C_B D,

and

    ‖v‖₂ ≤ √(|B|/c) A
             + C_B(1+√(M|B|/c)) D.

For example, the sum of these two coefficients is a permissible C(B,c,M). This proof gives explicit uniform dependence and does not require r to be bounded below pointwise.

A concrete Lean development should implement this lemma in two stages: (i) the L¹-to-H¹ upgrade with weak gradient and ordinary Poincaré; (ii) the weighted mean estimate using integral Cauchy–Schwarz and the almost-everywhere inequality r²≤Mr. The intermediate weak-derivative predicates must be defined by integration against compactly supported smooth tests. Their premises must not include the lemma's L² conclusion. The existing five declarations supply neither stage. Without checking the locked Mathlib source, I cannot honestly give executable API names for the Sobolev, mollification, and weak-compactness steps.

3. A uniform positive-mass anchor follows from the original class.

On [0,T], continuity into W^{1,q}, q>2, and planar Sobolev embedding give a uniform density bound M. Continuity into L¹ gives a uniform mass bound. The weighted velocity estimate implies

    ‖ρu‖₁ ≤ ‖ρ‖₁^(1/2) ‖√ρ u‖₂.

Choose a smooth cutoff χ equal to one on the unit ball and supported in the ball of radius two. Testing continuity with η(t)χ(x/L), the flux term is bounded by

    C L⁻¹ ‖η‖_{L¹_t} ‖ρu‖_{L∞_tL¹_x}.

It tends to zero. Dominated convergence in the density term shows that m(t)=∫ρ(t) has zero distributional time derivative. Its L¹-continuity makes m constant at every time in [0,T].

If m>0, compactness of the image of [0,T] in L¹ implies uniform tightness. For completeness, cover that image by finitely many L¹ balls of radius m/4 and choose one spatial ball containing all but m/4 of the mass of each center. Every density then has at least m/2 of its mass in that ball. Thus there are B₀ and c>0 with ∫_{B₀}ρ(t)≥c for all t.

This anchor is derived; it is not a positive-density hypothesis. If m=0, nonnegativity gives ρ(t)=0 almost everywhere for every t. Then fᵢ=P=0, and the conservative momentum equation directly gives the divergence-free viscous stress identity. No weighted coercivity is needed in that branch.

4. Local time regularity and the product rules.

Assume m>0 and interpretation (A). The distributional identity for ∇_xw, tested against separated time and space tests, yields the slice weak-gradient identity outside one null set. To justify this statement, use countably many determining spatial tests on each ball, intersect their full-measure sets, and extend by continuity of the pairings. Exhausting space by balls gives the identity simultaneously on all balls.

Apply the lemma of section 2 on every ball containing B₀ and integrate its squared estimate in time. The asserted bounds for ∇uₜ and √ρ uₜ give

    uₜ ∈ L²(0,T;H¹_loc(R²)).

The original velocity bounds give u ∈ L∞(0,T;H²_loc): local L² control follows from u ∈ L∞_t L^{q₂}_x with finite q₂, while first and second spatial derivatives are supplied by ∇u ∈ L∞_t H¹_x. Here a>1 implies α>1/2, so q₂=4/α is finite. Local planar H² embedding gives u ∈ L∞ on every smaller space-time cylinder.

Spatial weak product rules now give

    div(ρu)=u·∇ρ+ρ div u ∈ L∞_t L²_loc.

The conservative continuity equation therefore identifies

    ρₜ=−div(ρu) ∈ L∞_t L²_loc.

On a bounded spatial set, the functions and their temporal derivatives consequently belong to the requisite Bochner L² spaces. The temporal product rule can be proved directly rather than assumed: mollify ρ and u in time on an interior temporal interval. The smooth-in-time products satisfy

    ∂ₜ(ρ_ε uᵢ,ε)=ρₜ,ε uᵢ,ε+ρ_ε wᵢ,ε.

Each function and each derivative converges strongly in local L². For instance,

    ‖ρₜ,ε uᵢ,ε−ρₜuᵢ‖₁
       ≤ ‖ρₜ,ε−ρₜ‖₂ ‖uᵢ,ε‖₂
          + ‖ρₜ‖₂ ‖uᵢ,ε−uᵢ‖₂.

The right-hand side tends to zero; the other products have the same two-term estimate. Passing to distributions yields

    ∂ₜ(ρuᵢ)=ρₜuᵢ+ρwᵢ.

Spatial mollification, local Sobolev convergence, and the local boundedness of ρ and u prove

    div(ρuᵢu)=ρu·∇uᵢ+uᵢ div(ρu).

All terms are locally integrable. Combining these two proved identities with continuity cancels uᵢ(ρₜ+div(ρu)) and gives from the original conservative momentum equation

    ρ(wᵢ+u·∇uᵢ)=div Vᵢ

in space-time distributions, with exactly the stress row in the target. This cancellation uses no division by ρ.

5. Integrability and one common exceptional set.

The supplied fixed-time estimates are mathematically appropriate:

    ‖P‖₂ ≤ R‖ρ‖∞^(1/2)‖√ρ θ‖₂,
    ‖ρwᵢ‖₁ ≤ ‖ρ‖₁^(1/2)‖√ρ wᵢ‖₂,
    ‖ρu·∇uᵢ‖₁
       ≤ ‖ρ‖∞^(1/2)‖√ρ u‖₂‖∇uᵢ‖₂.

The gradient bounds give div u ∈ L∞_tL²_x. Hence fᵢ ∈ L∞_tL¹_x and Vᵢ ∈ L∞_tL²_x. These estimates do not assert unweighted global L² membership for u or θ.

For an integer n, let S_n be the smooth functions whose supports lie in the closed ball K_n of radius n. Equip S_n with the metric

    d_n(φ,ψ)=‖φ−ψ‖∞ + ‖∇φ−∇ψ‖∞.

It has a countable dense subset: the map φ↦(φ,∂₁φ,∂₂φ)|_{K_n} embeds it in the separable metric space C(K_n;R³). A subspace of a separable metric space is second countable and separable. Thus the dense family can be chosen inside S_n, preserving smoothness and support. This construction avoids assuming an arbitrary approximating family has a uniform support bound.

For each member φ of these countable families and each component, define

    Fᵢ,φ(t)=∫ fᵢ(t)φ + ∫ Vᵢ(t)·∇φ.

Fubini and the established bounds make Fᵢ,φ integrable on (0,T). The space-time identity gives ∫ηFᵢ,φ=0 for all temporal tests supported inside (0,T). The interval temporal-residual lemma therefore gives Fᵢ,φ=0 almost everywhere. Countable intersection, including the slice-integrability and derivative-identification sets, supplies a single exceptional set E.

At a time outside E, let φ_k→φ in the above metric, with all supports in K_n. Then

    |∫fᵢ(φ_k−φ)| ≤ ‖fᵢ‖₁‖φ_k−φ‖∞,

and

    |∫Vᵢ·∇(φ_k−φ)|
       ≤ ‖Vᵢ‖₂ |K_n|^(1/2)‖∇φ_k−∇φ‖∞.

Both vanish. Every smooth compactly supported test belongs to some S_n, so the weak identity holds for all such tests on this same time set. Applying the exact N0002 theorem then gives ∫fᵢ=0 for both components.

6. Exact formalization architecture and the first blocker.

A non-circular complete Lean development needs: a definition of the original solution class using weak derivatives and the original conservative equations; planar Sobolev embedding and local H² control; mass conservation and the uniform anchor; the weighted local coercivity lemma; derivative slicing; temporal and spatial weak product rules; Fubini for the residual pairings; separability of the supported smooth-test family and its extension estimate; and finally N0002.

The full theorem should quantify over such an original solution and conclude an almost-everywhere statement simultaneously containing integrability and the identity for every smooth compact test. Converting that almost-everywhere predicate to an explicit measurable null exceptional set is a measure-theoretic packaging step. Neither hdiv from the existing conditional theorem nor a product-rule field may be placed in the solution definition.

At the formal interface, the first blocker is that no full original-solution definition or common weak-time-derivative interface is supplied. Under the conventional derivative interpretation, the first missing analytic theorem in the proposed uₜ route is the weighted local coercivity lemma stated above, including its L¹-to-H¹ upgrade. Under the separate-limit interpretation, the earlier blocker is identification of those limits with a single regular distributional derivative; weighted coercivity cannot repair an undefined or incompatible weighted product. I do not provide fabricated compilable code for either blocker. The concrete proof architecture above specifies how to discharge them without assuming the desired cancellation.

【草案】补出了加权局部 Poincaré 的完整估计及 L¹ 到 H¹ 的升级路线，常数只依赖球、局部质量下界和密度上界，无需正密度下界。

formalizable_lemmas: Weighted local coercivity: on a bounded ball B, 0≤r≤M, ∫_B r≥c>0, v∈L¹(B), weak ∇v∈L²(B), and √r v∈L²(B) imply v∈H¹(B) and ‖v‖₂≤√(|B|/c)‖√r v‖₂+C_B(1+√(M|B|/c))‖∇v‖₂.

Mass-anchor lemma: nonnegative ρ continuous into L¹, an integrable uniformly bounded mass flux, and the distributional continuity equation imply constant mass; positive mass and compactness of the density trajectory give one ball carrying a uniform positive amount of mass.

Weak temporal product rule: locally L² functions a,b with locally L² distributional time derivatives A,B satisfy ∂_t(ab)=Ab+aB in distributions, proved by temporal mollification and L²×L²→L¹ convergence.
Spatial product rule at the derived regularity: ρ∈H¹_loc∩L∞_loc and u∈H²_loc in two dimensions imply div(ρu_i u)=ρu·∇u_i+u_i div(ρu), with locally integrable terms.

Common-test slicing lemma: space-time div identity with f_i∈L¹_tL¹_x and V_i∈L¹_tL²_x yields a single almost-everywhere time set on which the spatial identity holds for both components and all smooth compactly supported tests, using supported C¹-separable families.

Original-equation application: only after the preceding obligations are proved from the original solution-class definition, derive f_i=div V_i, obtain spatial L¹/L² membership, and apply the exact N0002 theorem.
